facts.statement: Principal-Protected Notes (PPNs): Structured product combining a zero-coupon bond guaranteeing return of principal at maturity T with a call option providing equity upside participation.

In Hull Section 12.1 PPN example: Risk-free rate = 6%, 3-year term. Present value of $1,000 principal = 1000 * exp(-0.06 * 3) = $835.27. Remaining $164.73 ($1,000 - $835.27) purchases at-the-money call options.

Covered Call vs. Protective Put: Covered Call (Long Stock + Short Call) trades away upside above strike K in exchange for upfront income. Protective Put (Long Stock + Long Put) buys downside insurance while preserving upside.

Bull Call Spread: Long Call with lower strike K1 (cost c1) + Short Call with higher strike K2 (income c2). Max Profit = (K2 - K1) - Net Debit. Max Loss = Net Debit = c1 - c2. Breakeven = K1 + Net Debit.

Hull Section 12.2 Bull Spread Example: Buy Call K1 = $30 for c1 = $3.00, Sell Call K2 = $35 for c2 = $1.00. Net Debit = $2.00. Max Profit = ($35 - $30) - $2 = $3.00. Max Loss = $2.00. Breakeven = $30 + $2 = $32.00.
Bear Spread: Designed to profit from moderately falling prices. Bear Put Spread (Debit): Buy Put K2, Sell Put K1. Bear Call Spread (Credit): Sell Call K1, Buy Call K2.

Box Spread: Combination of Bull Call Spread (strikes K1, K2) + Bear Put Spread (strikes K1, K2). Payoff is identically equal to K2 - K1 at maturity in ALL economic states, replicating a pure risk-free zero-coupon bond. Value today = (K2 - K1) * exp(-r*T).

Greeks Dynamics in Vertical Spreads: Delta is positive for Bull spreads, negative for Bear spreads. Gamma and Vega peak when underlying price is near active strikes and decay rapidly toward expiration.
